subject: BrightMed onboarding: acceptance evidence, load test plan, and ramp notes
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@brightmed.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightMed onboarding: acceptance evidence, load test plan, and ramp notes

Hi Laura / BrightMed team,

The attached load test plan (brightmed_load_plan_v1.xlsx) is our first-pass proposal for the acceptance run and evidence we need to sign off the onboarding milestone. High-level items below — please review and tell us which of these you want to prioritize in the first window:

- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms for 95% of traffic shapes; burst tail allowance to 350ms for short spikes.
- Throughput target: sustained 400 req/s for the primary route (chat.complete); peak ramp to 1.2k req/s for 2-minute bursts.
- Synthetic vs. production shadowing: we recommend doing both. Start with synthetic load to validate resource sizing, then a short (30m) shadow run against preprod with sampled real traffic.
- Error budget: <1% 5xx during acceptance window; transient 429s tolerated for <0.5% of tokens.
- Evidence: k6 load scripts, raw latency histograms, KV-cache hit rates, GPU utilization traces, and a short postmortem if thresholds are missed.

Dev, can you confirm the exact k6 profile and any environment variables we should provide the BrightMed team? Grace, I'll need your acceptance checklist added to the doc (data retention, logs access, evidence retention window).

Next steps: Laura, if this plan looks reasonable, can you confirm a target week for the acceptance window? We can run the synthetic pass the week of 06/28 and schedule the shadow at your earliest convenience.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: brightmed_load_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet; test scenarios and resource matrix)
From: Laura Chen <laura@brightmed.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMed TechOps <techops@brightmed.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:30:47 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightMed onboarding: acceptance evidence, load test plan, and ramp notes

Thanks Olga — appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) On latency SLOs: can you confirm these are measured at the gateway-to-model end-to-end (including our proxy) or strictly at the Redwood model endpoint? We want to know what to include in our internal dashboards.
2) For the shadow run, will you be able to provide a tokenized sample of our live requests so we can replay realistic sequences in preprod, or should we generate synthetic traces on our side?
3) Evidence retention: we need the raw traces for 30 days; is that possible to store in the shared drive or provide as a zipped artifact after the run?

Target week: we were hoping for the week of 06/28 as well. If the synthetic run is quick and the shadow won't interfere with our other QA activities, that works. Our TechOps prefers morning runs (08:00–12:00 PT).

Laura Chen
Program Manager, Platform
BrightMed
laura@brightmed.com

Laura — quick answers from an engineering standpoint and the exact commands we'll hand over: 

- Measurement point: Redwood will provide measurements at the model endpoint (post-ingress, pre-response), plus an ingress timer so you can compute gateway+model latency. We'll supply combined and endpoint-only histograms.

- Replay data: we can accept a tokenized request log (stripped of PHI/PPI) and convert to k6-compatible payloads. If you can't provide that, our synthetic generator will approximate session timing and prompt lengths.

- Storage: we'll upload raw artifacts to the shared onboarding Drive (30 days retention) and provide a zipped download. If you require longer retention, we can add an export to your S3.

Engineer-run commands (attached as engineer_test_commands.md in this thread):

k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m --out json=brightmed_synthetic_200vus.json scripts/brightmed_synthetic.js

# for a peak ramp test (short burst)
k6 run --vus 1200 --duration 2m --out json=brightmed_burst_1200vus.json scripts/brightmed_burst.js

Notes: start with the 200 VUs sustained run to validate cache warm-up and batching behavior; the burst run is intended to validate autoscaling and tail latency. We'll provide k6 scripts with header templates and an auth helper.

I'll attach the command file to the Drive. Olga — can you confirm whether BrightMed needs a RedTeam time window (we'll suppress rate-limits to mimic production for the shadow)?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: engineer_test_commands.md (k6 commands and env var list)

Adding acceptance criteria and compliance notes here so we're all aligned. Short checklist that we'll use to mark pass/fail after the run: 

- Performance: p95 latency measured at the Redwood endpoint must be <= 220ms for the sustained scenario and <= 350ms for the burst tail. Tokenization artefacts excluded.
- Reliability: <1% server errors (5xx) across all scenarios.
- Autoscaling: no more than a single scale-step delay leading to >5s queueing on average for the burst test.
- Observability: artifacts uploaded within 4 hours of run completion to the onboarding Drive (histograms, GPU metrics, KV hit rate, request logs).
- Privacy/compliance: any replayed request logs must be de-identified and accompanied by a signed data handling attestation from BrightMed.

If everything above is okay, we'll plan for the synthetic run on 2027-06-28 at 09:00 PT and the shadow on 2027-06-29 at 08:30 PT (morning windows per your Ops note). Please confirm.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: BrightMed onboarding: acceptance evidence, load test plan, and ramp notes

Olga / team — quick sync and results from this week's runs. Attached is the zipped evidence bundle (brightmed_load_evidence_20270625.zip) with the k6 JSON outputs and ingress histograms. Summary: 

- Synthetic sustained (200 VUs, 30m): p50 52ms, p95 195ms, p99 310ms. 5xx: 0.3%. KV-hit steady at ~68%. GPU avg util 72%.
- Burst (1200 VUs, 2m): p50 68ms, p95 260ms, p99 410ms. Short spikes up to 560ms observed on two host nodes during peak second 30s; these were correlated with an autoscaling lag while the nodes spun up. No data loss observed.
- Shadow run (sampled): average end-to-end p95 ~230ms (includes our ingress proxy); Redwood endpoint-only p95 ~200ms.

Conclusion: Based on the acceptance checklist, BrightMed accepts the synthetic run results as passing for the sustained scenario. The burst test shows a marginal exceed at p99 during two short segments — we'll request a remediation item to tune autoscaling thresholds and retry backoff settings before GA.

We've uploaded the artifacts to the shared onboarding Drive and left a copy in our internal S3 bucket. Let us know if you need any additional extracts.

Thanks,
BrightMed TechOps
techops@brightmed.com

Attachment: brightmed_load_evidence_20270625.zip (k6 outputs, histograms, node traces)
